slides.title: DataFrames & Series
slides.content:
# Excel for Python 📊

## Series
A 1D labeled array (like a column).
```python
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30])
```

## DataFrame
A 2D table with rows and columns.
```python
data = {
    'Name': ['Alice', 'Bob'],
    'Age': [25, 30]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
```

slides.title: Reading Data
slides.content:
# I/O Superpowers 📥

Pandas can read almost anything.

```python
# CSV
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Excel
df = pd.read_excel('data.xlsx')

# JSON
df = pd.read_json('data.json')

# HTML Tables (scrapes web!)
dfs = pd.read_html('https://en.wikipedia.org/...')
```

slides.title: Data Inspection
slides.content:
# Sneak Peek 👀

Once data is loaded:

- `df.head(5)`: View first 5 rows.
- `df.info()`: Check data types and missing values.
- `df.describe()`: Statistical summary (mean, max, min) for numeric columns.
- `df.shape`: (rows, cols) tuple.

slides.quizQuestion: Which method gives you technical info like data types and null counts?

slides.title: Analysis & Cleaning
slides.content:
# Wrangling Data 🤠

## Filtering
```python
# People older than 25
adults = df[df['Age'] > 25]
```

## Grouping
Like SQL GROUP BY.
```python
# Average salary by Department
df.groupby('Dept')['Salary'].mean()
```

## Missing Data
```python
df.dropna() # Drop rows with missing values
df.fillna(0) # Fill missing with 0
```
